meta.source: Spider (Yu et al., 2018) dev-split questions + official gold SQL (combined_data.parquet), verbatim -- third-party authored, not hand-written for this project.
meta.purpose: Held-out evaluation domain: a Spider database no system, prompt or engine fix was developed on. Built mechanically by heldout/build_domains.py under the rule fixed in heldout/PREREGISTRATION.md before any held-out cell ran.
meta.selection_note: 38 Spider questions covering 19 distinct gold queries, deduplicated by exact gold SQL text (first phrasing kept). Every distinct query kept; none authored, reworded, dropped or padded.
meta.register_rule: the table the most deduplicated questions read alone, ties to more rows then name: {'employee': 4, 'shop': 7, 'hiring': 1, 'evaluation': 1}
meta.tiers: Mechanical (heldout/sql_tier.py): out_of_scope_register if the gold SQL reads any table other than the register; else out_of_contract_aggregate if it uses a construct outside the Goal vocabulary (architectural_gap lists each); else the SQL structure (filter/aggregate/group_by/order_by), the answer tier.
meta.tier_convention_note: As in the released Spider corpora: out_of_scope_register questions are answerable in principle but need a table outside the register (expected_behavior=refuse); out_of_contract_aggregate questions are in scope by tau and excluded from scoring because the Goal vocabulary cannot express them (expected_behavior=answer, gold executed).

queries.gold_sql: SELECT name FROM employee ORDER BY age

queries.question: What is the number of employees from each city?
queries.gold_sql: SELECT count(*) ,  city FROM employee GROUP BY city
queries.reason: reads table(s) ['employee'] -- this domain's single-table register only exposes 'shop'; the data this question needs is not visible to the system.

queries.question: Which cities do more than one employee under age 30 come from?
queries.gold_sql: SELECT city FROM employee WHERE age  <  30 GROUP BY city HAVING count(*)  >  1

queries.question: Find the number of shops in each location.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT count(*) ,  LOCATION FROM shop GROUP BY LOCATION

queries.question: Find the manager name and district of the shop whose number of products is the largest.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT manager_name ,  district FROM shop ORDER BY number_products DESC LIMIT 1

queries.question: find the minimum and maximum number of products of all stores.
Return the name, location and district of all shops in descending order of number of products.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT name ,  LOCATION ,  district FROM shop ORDER BY number_products DESC

queries.question: Find the names of stores whose number products is more than the average number of products.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT name FROM shop WHERE number_products  >  (SELECT avg(number_products) FROM shop)

queries.question: find the name of employee who was awarded the most times in the evaluation.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT t1.name FROM employee AS t1 JOIN evaluation AS t2 ON t1.Employee_ID  =  t2.Employee_ID GROUP BY t2.Employee_ID ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1
queries.reason: reads table(s) ['employee', 'evaluation'] -- this domain's single-table register only exposes 'shop'; the data this question needs is not visible to the system.

queries.question: Find the name of the employee who got the highest one time bonus.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT t1.name FROM employee AS t1 JOIN evaluation AS t2 ON t1.Employee_ID  =  t2.Employee_ID ORDER BY t2.bonus DESC LIMIT 1
queries.reason: reads table(s) ['employee', 'evaluation'] -- this domain's single-table register only exposes 'shop'; the data this question needs is not visible to the system.

queries.question: Find the names of employees who never won any award in the evaluation.
